$comment: LUC MEDIA RATE CARD — THE CUSTOMER PRICE, AND ONLY THE CUSTOMER PRICE.
HARD RULE (owner-stated, 2026-08-18): this file states the price WE CHARGE per
generation. It must NEVER carry an underlying/wholesale/vendor cost, a margin, or
a rate factor. There is deliberately no `wholesale*`, no `cost*`, no `margin*`, no
`platformRateFactor` key here, and none may ever be added — lib/luc/no-leak.test.ts
(Broad|Cast) and media-ctg.leak.test.ts (AIMS) fail the build if one appears.
This mirrors the precedent already set in the AIMS repo by commit 2c305a68,
'strip internal economics from /luc/pricing — no wholesale rates, no
platformRateFactor', and by sqlite-ledger.ts::ledgerEntries(), which deliberately
never SELECTs the internal `model` column.
UNIT: every rate is in LUC UNITS. 1 LUC Unit = $0.01 USD (AIMS
backend/uef-gateway/src/luc/pricing.ts, LUC_USD). Verified identical to the
'credits' unit of aims-tools/luc/luc.constants.ts SERVICE_CATALOG — see
provenance note `unit-identity` below.
THIS FILE IS BYTE-IDENTICAL IN TWO REPOS:
BoomerAng9/AIMS            backend/uef-gateway/src/luc/media-rate-card.json  (CANON)
BoomerAng9/broad-cast-app  lib/luc/media-rate-card.json                      (MIRROR)
A sha256 drift test in each repo fails if they diverge.

proof: backend/uef-gateway/src/luc/pricing.ts LANES.standard.outPlatformPer1k = 3.0 LUC per 1000 tokens = 0.003 LUC/token. Exact match.
SERVICE_CATALOG.llm_tokens_in.defaultRate = 0.001 credits/token; LANES.frontier.inPlatformPer1k = 1.0 LUC per 1000 tokens = 0.001 LUC/token. Exact match.

Both SERVICE_CATALOG LLM rows land exactly on an existing v6 platform-lane value, so the two tables share one unit. SERVICE_CATALOG is the lane-agnostic default table; pricing.ts is the lane-aware one.
unitIdentity.verifiedBy: media-ctg.unit-identity.test.ts (asserts the arithmetic against the real pricing.ts LANES table, not against a copied number)

reconciliationFlags.finding: SERVICE_CATALOG.voice_chars.defaultRate = 0.00001 credits/char. At the verified 1 credit = $0.01 that is $0.0000001/char = $0.10 per MILLION characters — roughly three orders of magnitude below any real voice-synthesis reference. NOT adopted as the voice CTG rate.
reconciliationFlags.action: voice priced per delivered audio-second instead (voice.per_audio_second), which is also the unit the delivered artifact can actually be measured in.

reconciliationFlags.finding: SERVICE_CATALOG.container_hours = 0.05 credits/hour but node_runtime_seconds = 0.0001 credits/second = 0.36 credits/hour — 7.2x apart for two compute meters, and 0.05 credits/hour = $0.0005/hour is far below any real container cost. Neither is reconciled to the v6 Tesla Matrix.
reconciliationFlags.action: no infrastructure row from SERVICE_CATALOG is used as a media rate. compute.gpu_second is stated fresh and marked proposed.

reconciliationFlags.finding: SERVICE_CATALOG's two LLM rows ARE canon-aligned (see unitIdentity). Only the non-LLM rows are unreconciled.
reconciliationFlags.action: token line items on a media receipt are priced by the real canonical missionBurnLuc() from pricing.ts, never by a number stated here.

$comment: CANON. These are the PLATFORM (customer-price) columns of the v6 Tesla Matrix
burn table, copied verbatim from backend/uef-gateway/src/luc/pricing.ts LANES:
inPlatformPer1k -> inLucPer1k, outPlatformPer1k -> outLucPer1k.
The wholesale columns of that same table (inWholesalePer1k / outWholesalePer1k) and
PLATFORM_RATE_FACTOR are DELIBERATELY ABSENT and must never be added — this mirror
is structurally incapable of carrying our vendor economics.
media-ctg.canon.test.ts in the AIMS repo asserts these equal the real LANES table.

rates.label: Generation time
rates.derivation: 0.25 LUC/s = $0.0025/s = $9.00 per generation-hour. Stated fresh rather than taken from SERVICE_CATALOG, whose two infrastructure rows contradict each other and are unreconciled to the v6 Tesla Matrix (see reconciliationFlags). Sized so that a real measured still on our own box (512x512, 4 steps, 2.6-8s wall — real range recorded in brain/okf/stargate/broadcast-media-wiring.md Part 5) lands near the stills.per_image + stills.per_megapixel unit price, so the time line and the unit line agree in order of magnitude instead of one swamping the other.
rates.ownerQuestion: Confirm $9.00/generation-hour as the retail rate for time on the self-hosted generation plane, or state the rate you want.

rates.label: Still image
rates.derivation: Flat per-artifact component, 2 LUC = $0.02. Affordability check against canon (pricing.ts TIERS): the Medium tier is 2000 LUC/month, so a 512x512 4-step still at the full line-item total below (~7.4 LUC) is ~270 stills/month on Medium.
rates.ownerQuestion: Confirm ~270 stills/month on the $19.99 Medium tier is the intended generosity, or state the per-still price you want.

rates.label: Image resolution
rates.derivation: Scales price with the real requested/delivered pixel area, which is the input that actually drives generation cost. 512x512 = 0.262 MP = 1.05 LUC; 1024x1024 = 1.049 MP = 4.19 LUC.
rates.ownerQuestion: Confirm resolution scaling is linear in pixel area at 4 LUC/MP.

rates.label: Refinement passes
rates.derivation: Step count is the other real driver of generation time and is a real, user-visible quality control. 0.1 LUC/step; the proven default workflow uses 4 steps = 0.4 LUC.

rates.label: Motion
rates.derivation: 40 LUC/s = $0.40 per delivered second of video. Video is by far the most expensive lane. Affordability check against canon: Medium (2000 LUC/mo) buys ~50 seconds/month; Superior (8000 LUC/mo) buys ~200 seconds/month.
rates.ownerQuestion: Confirm $0.40 per delivered video-second. NOTE: the Motion lane is NOT yet proven from this app (only Stills and Voice have real end-to-end proof) — this rate is priced but not yet exercised.

rates.label: Voice & Sound
rates.derivation: 0.5 LUC/s = $0.005 per delivered audio-second = $0.30 per audio-minute. Replaces SERVICE_CATALOG.voice_chars, which is implausible by ~3 orders of magnitude (see reconciliationFlags). Affordability check against canon: Medium (2000 LUC/mo) buys ~66 minutes of speech/month.

estimationModel.$comment: Seed constants for the PRE-flight estimate only. Every one of these is replaced by a real rolling median from this tenant's own settled receipts as soon as enough real history exists (see historyMinSamples). They are seeds, not prices.

seedGpuSeconds.$comment: Seeded from the real measured range recorded in brain/okf/stargate/broadcast-media-wiring.md Part 5 (2.6-8s for a 512x512 4-step still on the real box) and from this task's own measured runs. Superseded by real per-tenant history.

seedSpeakingCharsPerSecond.$comment: Used ONLY to estimate audio duration from a script before the audio exists. NOT YET MEASURED on our own voice plane — an attempt was made during this work and the Voice & Sound lane returned a real upstream 502 (capability advertised implemented+configured by the proxy, but /v1/media/dispatch failed), so no honest measurement was possible. This value is therefore a DERIVED seed, stated openly: ~150 words/min of natural English speech x ~5.1 characters per word including the trailing space = 12.75 characters/second. It is superseded by this tenant's real measured history as soon as historyMinSamples real voice runs exist, so it stops mattering after the third successful generation. Tracked as GAP-LUC-003.
